## Home-Care Plan for Sore Throat, Congestion, and Dry Cough

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg

Your symptoms for 3 days without fever fit a common pattern of **viral upper respiratory irritation, allergies, or both**. With mild reflux in the mix, throat irritation and dry cough can also be made worse by stomach acid.

## Safer Over-the-Counter Choices With Reflux

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg

- **For congestion:** a **non-drowsy antihistamine** may help if allergies are contributing; these are generally easier on reflux than many “cold/flu” combo products.
- **For throat irritation / dry cough:** **honey**, lozenges, warm tea, and humidified air are low-risk options and often help more than strong cough suppressants for mild symptoms.
- **For pain or throat discomfort:** **acetaminophen** is usually gentler on the stomach than many NSAIDs.
- **For reflux-related throat symptoms:** an **antacid or acid-reducing medicine** may help if you notice burning, sour taste, or symptoms worse after meals or at night.
- **Use caution with:** multi-symptom cold medicines, decongestants, and NSAIDs if they tend to worsen your reflux, dry you out, or raise your heart rate.

### Quick reflux-friendly guidance
- Choose **single-ingredient** products when possible.
- Avoid taking medicines on an empty stomach if the label says food may help.
- Try not to lie down right after eating or after taking anything that can irritate your stomach.
- If your cough is mostly from throat tickle, soothing measures may be enough.

## When to See a Clinician

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/phone.svg

Seek medical care sooner if you develop any of these:
- **Trouble breathing, wheezing, chest pain, or blue lips**
- **High fever**, or fever that starts after several days of symptoms
- **Severe sore throat** with trouble swallowing, drooling, or muffled voice
- **Symptoms lasting more than about 10 days**, or improving then getting worse again
- **Thick facial pain/pressure** or worsening one-sided sinus pain
- **Signs of dehydration** such as dizziness, very dark urine, or inability to keep fluids down
- **Coughing up blood**, or a cough that becomes significantly worse
- **Concern for strep, COVID, or flu exposure**, especially if symptoms change quickly

## Simple At-Home Steps That Usually Help

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/moon-stars.svg

- Drink fluids often; warm drinks can soothe throat irritation.
- Use saline nasal spray or rinse for congestion.
- Run a humidifier or take a steamy shower.
- Rest your voice and avoid smoke, strong fragrances, and very dry air.
- For reflux, eat smaller meals and avoid late-night eating, heavy/fatty foods, alcohol, and lying flat soon after meals.
- If allergies are active, reducing exposure to pollen and dust can make both congestion and cough better.

## Sources

- NHS: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/common-cold/
- Mayo Clinic: https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/common-cold/diagnosis-treatment/drc-20351611
- Cleveland Clinic: https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/21153-laryngopharyngeal-reflux-lpr
